faqs.question: What does AFB Identification & Speciation (MTB and MOTT) Test measure?
faqs.answer: This test identifies Mycobacteria species present in your sample.

faqs.question: Why is AFB Identification & Speciation (MTB and MOTT) Test done?
faqs.answer: • To identify Mycobacteria species, including the bacteria responsible for tuberculosis (MTB) and other non-tuberculous mycobacteria (MOTT) • To evaluate the effectiveness of treatment • To diagnose and monitor infections • To assess the risk of developing complications

faqs.question: When is AFB Identification & Speciation (MTB and MOTT) Test recommended, and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: • This test is recommended for patients who have symptoms suggestive of tuberculosis or pulmonary infections. • It may also be advised for individuals with a history of exposure to tuberculosis, those with a persistent cough, fever, weight loss, or abnormal chest X-ray findings.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB Identification & Speciation (MTB and MOTT) Test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may indicate the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis or other non-tuberculous mycobacterial infections.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB Identification & Speciation (MTB and MOTT) Test?
faqs.answer: A healthcare professional will collect a sample of your sputum, bronchial washings, or other respiratory secretions. They will send the sample to the laboratory for testing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB Identification & Speciation (MTB and MOTT) Test?
faqs.answer: • Follow any instructions provided by your doctor regarding fasting, medication, or other specific preparations. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with AFB Identification & Speciation (MTB and MOTT) Test?
faqs.answer: • Acid-fast bacilli smear: To detect acid-fast bacteria like Mycobacterium tuberculosis • Drug susceptibility testing: To determine which antibiotics are effective against the detected Mycobacteria species

faqs.question: What is the AFB Identification & Speciation (MTB and MOTT) Test also known as?
faqs.answer: Mycobacterial Identification and Speciation Test or Tuberculosis Culture Test

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is a contagious infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also impact other organs. Common symptoms include a persistent cough, weight loss, fever, night sweats, and fatigue. TB is treatable with appropriate medications.
